claims.text: A physics-informed machine-learning framework can accurately predict low phonon thermal conductivity in single-phase high-entropy alloys.
Integrating ab initio anharmonic force constants with compositional-disorder descriptors will improve phonon thermal-conductivity prediction.
The proposed framework will provide more than a 25% improvement in predictive accuracy over empirical or semi-empirical scattering models.
The intended materials are single-phase, disordered, multi-principal-element high-entropy alloys formulated for thermal insulation.
The model will be trained on ab initio anharmonic force constants and disorder descriptors and calibrated with mode-resolved phonon-lifetime measurements.
Combining computational modeling with experimental calibration can improve model or database accuracy in high-entropy-alloy research.
The approach applies from ambient to moderately high temperatures when phonon conduction dominates.
The approach applies only while the alloy remains a uniform disordered solution without phase separation or ordering.
Compositional disorder and anharmonic phonon-phonon interactions mediate phonon thermal transport in the target alloys.
Physics-based descriptors capture effects of anharmonic lattice dynamics and disorder-induced scattering that traditional models oversimplify.
Capturing anharmonicity and disorder-induced scattering produces more accurate relationships between composition, microstructure, and phonon transport.
The framework will predict phonon thermal conductivity within 25% of experimental measurements under the designated conditions.
The framework will significantly reduce prediction error relative to current empirical or semi-empirical models.
Predictive performance is not guaranteed for alloys containing significant secondary phases.
Predictive performance is not guaranteed when electronic or other non-phonon heat-conduction mechanisms dominate.
Comprehensive experimental data for single-phase high-entropy alloys are limited.
Comprehensive mode-resolved phonon-lifetime data are limited across relevant compositions and temperatures.
Inelastic neutron scattering can provide the mode-resolved phonon lifetimes required by the proposed benchmark.
Laser-flash analysis or an equivalent method can provide the complementary macroscopic thermal-conductivity measurements.
Prediction errors exceeding 25% for a statistically significant number of samples under the defined conditions would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The headline claim is a greater-than-25% improvement relative to baseline models, whereas the outcome and falsification rule use an absolute prediction error of 25%. These are different performance criteria: a model can be within 25% of experiment without improving on the baseline by more than 25%, or can improve by more than 25% while still having an error above 25%.
